exceptions.warning: NO day-count convention is stated anywhere in original_agreement.pdf, amendment_1.pdf, waiver_1.pdf, or any other executed document in the deal folder (confirmed by full-text sweep). actual/360 with both endpoints counted is recorded here purely as the engine's supported default / market-standard assumption, NOT a stated term.

MATERIAL, larger than the usual stub-day question: the borrower's own certified monthly Cash Flow / Debt Roll-Forward figures show (Cash interest / Beginning debt) x 12 converging to the SAME ~10.2551136% annualized rate to 9-10 significant figures in EVERY month checked (2025-01 through 2026-05), regardless of whether that month has 28, 29, 30, or 31 calendar days (e.g. February 2025 (28 days), March 2025 (31 days) and April 2025 (30 days) all imply the identical rate to 9 significant figures). This is only possible if the certified figures are computed on a FLAT (annual rate)/12 monthly-equivalent basis (a 30/360 bond-basis-style convention) with NO variation for actual days elapsed -- not on any real actual/360 or actual/365 day count. debt_service.py v1 supports only 'actual/360' or 'actual/365' with REAL calendar-day counting, and has no flat/30-360-bond-basis mode. EXPECT the generated schedule's cash-interest figures to NOT tie to the certified monthly figures in ANY ordinary (non-stub) month -- the direction and size of the gap will vary with the number of days in each calendar month (larger in 31-day months, smaller in 28-day months, versus the certified figure's flat treatment).

FUNDING-MONTH STUB (January 2025): the borrower's own certified reporting books a FULL month of accrued interest ($1,049,562.06) and a full month of required principal for January 2025 despite the mid-month (January 15) Closing Date, with no visible proration for the resulting stub period. The engine, by contrast, computes January's accrual only from the actual funding date (2025-01-15) forward (17 days inclusive of both endpoints, out of 31) -- layered on top of the flat-vs-actual-day-count gap above, not a substitute for it.

VERIFIED BY RUNNING THE GENERATOR (--as-of 2026-06): generated cash_interest_accrued is $594,751.83 for 2025-01 (17-day stub) against the certified $1,049,562.06 (full month) -- a ~43% shortfall in the stub month alone, exactly as predicted above. In ordinary (non-stub) months the direction of the gap flips with month length, also exactly as predicted: $977,632.07 generated for 2025-02 (28 days) vs. certified $1,047,462.93 (engine LOWER, because 28/360 < the certified figure's implicit 30/360), but $1,080,209.27 generated for 2025-03 (31 days) vs. certified $1,045,368.01 (engine HIGHER, because 31/360 > 30/360). No single generated month in the schedule ties the certified figure to the cent; treat the generated cash-interest row as a reasonable annual-run-rate approximation only, not a month-by-month substitute for the certified figures.

Recommend obtaining the full executed credit agreement (if one exists beyond this data room's one-page excerpt of original_agreement.pdf) to confirm the true day-count convention, rate, margin/index, and funding-month proration language before relying on this generated schedule for anything beyond an approximation.
